evidence.requirements: All brief items are met. The start page lists title, date/time, price per guest and "<n> seats left" (Home.tsx:35-41, format.ts:11, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (Home.tsx:43-45). The form has Name/Email/Guests (1-8) and a Book button (Booking.tsx:132-168). Seat limit is enforced on the server (store.ts:59-60) and errors show next to the field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (Booking.tsx:209-233, confirmation.jpg). /staff has Password/Sign in, uses STAFF_PASSWORD, groups bookings by tasting and has a Cancel button that frees seats (Staff.tsx, app.ts:153-183, staff.jpg). Uses React, Express, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. PORT defaults to 3000 (index.ts:4); bookings are in memory. One judgement call: when a tasting is fully booked the "Book <title>" link is hidden and a "Fully booked" badge shows instead (Home.tsx:42). That is a reasonable reading of 'each tasting has a link'.
evidence.correctness: Checking seats and inserting the booking happen in one synchronous step (store.ts:55-70), and a concurrent test proves exactly one of two requests wins (bookings.test.ts:102-110). Seats left are derived from bookings, so a cancel frees seats (store.ts:33-37, 72). Boundaries are covered by tests: 1 and 8 guests, 0, 9, 2.5, '1e1' and NaN (booking-schema.test.ts:38-44). Booking exactly the remaining seats works (store.test.ts:35-45). The client caps max at the seats left and refines the schema (Booking.tsx:73-85). On a 409 it shows the server error next to Guests and reloads the tasting (Booking.tsx:104-111). A ref guard stops double submits (Booking.tsx:119-126). Unknown and repeated cancels return 404. Minor: the confirmation lives only in component state, so it is lost on reload. The overview prints "1 seats left" (the brief's literal format).
evidence.security: The password is compared in constant time over SHA-256 digests (app.ts:29-33). Sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset. Login has a rate limit of 10 failures per 15 minutes (app.ts:75-82). The cookie-session cookie is signed with a random key, httpOnly and sameSite=strict, with secure opt-in (app.ts:55-64). Forged cookies are rejected in a test (staff.test.ts:62-67). POSTs must be JSON (415 otherwise) with a 10kb body limit (app.ts:35-41, 73), plus helmet CSP and Cache-Control no-store. React escapes all output and there are no secrets in the code. Small gap: the session is stateless, so a captured cookie stays valid until maxAge (8h) even after logout.
evidence.code_quality: Clear split: shared zod schema used by both client and server (shared/booking.ts), a small store, an Express app factory, and pages and components. Naming is good, types are explicit, and errors map to fields consistently. Minor blemishes: a formatting glitch at Staff.tsx:176 (`{tastings.map((tasting) => (            <section`). The custom useLoad hook (useLoad.ts) is a bit clever. The fake API's 409 text duplicates and drifts from the server's (fakeApi.ts:52-53 vs app.ts:138-141).
evidence.tests: Coverage is broad and meaningful. Unit tests cover the schema and the store. Supertest API tests cover validation, 409 on seats, concurrency, rate limits, the auth flow, forged cookies, cancel/404 and caching headers. React Testing Library tests cover the form errors linked via aria-describedby, the confirmation, fully booked, staff cancel and session expiry. Playwright e2e runs on desktop and at 360px phone width, with axe checks, horizontal-scroll checks and 44px touch-target checks (e2e/quality.spec.ts). test-results/.last-run.json shows passed. Small weakness: the UI tests use a hand-written fake API whose messages differ from the server's (booking.test.tsx:102 asserts "Only 1 seats are left").
evidence.ux_design: A coherent winery look: wine-red header with a gold rule, cream paper background and serif headings (start.jpg). Cards have a clear hierarchy of date, title, price, seats left and a CTA. The form error state has a red border, tint, icon and message (form.jpg). Success uses a green panel with a check mark (confirmation.jpg). Weaknesses: dates are raw '2026-11-06 18:00' (a weekday label helps). There is no imagery or description of each tasting. Staff Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation (Staff.tsx:203-210).
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a label, and errors use aria-invalid, aria-describedby and role=alert (Booking.tsx:173-178, Feedback.tsx:31-40). Focus goes to the first error (shouldFocusError, setFocus). There is a skip link and a gold focus-visible outline (Layout.tsx:19-24, index.css:41-44). Pages use landmarks and articles labelled by their headings, and Banner uses alert or status roles. axe checks run on every page in e2e. Muted text (#5c4f53) has good contrast. Gaps: the staff Cancel buttons are all named just 'Cancel' with no booking context for screen readers (Staff.tsx:203-210). The seat meter is aria-hidden, which is fine because the text duplicates it.
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies fit the problem (Express, cookie-session, react-hook-form, zod, React Router, Tailwind). Helmet and express-rate-limit add a little but are justified. The trust-proxy option and the custom useLoad hook add some surface. About 1,000 lines of app code is appropriate.
evidence.maintainability: README covers run/dev/test commands, environment variables (STAFF_PASSWORD, TRUST_PROXY, COOKIE_SECURE) and the folder layout. CONSTRAINTS.md documents the quality gates. There are lint, typecheck, unit and e2e scripts, and package-lock.json is present. Missing: no CI pipeline configuration. README says `openspec/` holds 'the specification, design and task list', but only openspec/specs/.gitkeep exists. No ADRs, no staff manual, no changelog or release approach. The runtime is only `engines: >=22` with no .nvmrc. Dependency ranges use carets (the lockfile mitigates this).
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent (Georgia serif headings, system sans body). The palette is restrained (wine, gold, parchment, leaf green for success, red for danger) and buttons are consistent across all four screenshots. It looks finished and on-brand, though fairly plain: no photos, a small grape icon, and the empty seat bars look like blank strips when nothing is booked (start.jpg).
evidence.layout: The start page leads with the hero heading, then a three-column card grid with aligned CTAs (start.jpg). The form is centred and narrow, with the price aligned right opposite the date (form.jpg). The confirmation card is compact with a dl grid (confirmation.jpg). The staff page groups bookings in per-tasting cards, with the seats-left count top right and Cancel aligned right (staff.jpg). No overlap or clipping is visible. Each staff booking takes four rows, which gets tall with many bookings.
evidence.usability: Guests finish in two steps: Book link, then the form with a sensible default of 2 guests and a hint '1 to 8 guests, EUR 28 each' (form.jpg). The confirmation offers a 'Back to the tastings' link. Fully booked state is clear on both the card and the form. Staff get Refresh and Sign out, a success notice after a cancel, and recovery from an expired session. The main friction is the one-click irreversible Cancel. Fully booked tastings show no hint of a waitlist or contact option.
evidence.reception: Guests would see it as a trustworthy, tidy winery booking page with a clear booking reference. The tone is friendly ('Join us in the cellar…'). Staff get a usable list. It would feel more inviting with descriptions of each tasting and human-readable dates, but it is professional enough to use and recommend.

unmet_requirements: Partly: when a tasting is fully booked its "Book <tasting title>" link is removed (Home.tsx:42), so not every tasting always has the link. A Fully booked badge appears instead, which is a reasonable reading of the brief.
strengths: The server enforces the seat limit with an atomic check-and-insert and proves it with a concurrency test. The shared zod schema gives field-level errors that match on client and server.
Solid security for the scope: SHA-256 plus timingSafeEqual password check, login rate limit, signed httpOnly sameSite=strict session, JSON-only POSTs, helmet and no-store caching.
Thorough tests across unit, API, component and Playwright e2e on desktop and 360px phone, with axe, overflow and touch-target checks, inside a coherent, polished winery theme.
issues: Maintainability gaps: there is no CI pipeline, and README points to an openspec/ specification that is empty (only .gitkeep). There are also no ADRs, no staff manual and no release approach.
Staff 'Cancel' is irreversible, fires with no confirmation, and every button has the same accessible name with no booking context (Staff.tsx:203-210).

Guest-facing polish: dates appear as raw '2026-11-06 18:00', tastings have no description, and the confirmation is lost on page reload. The UI test fake API also drifts from the real server messages (fakeApi.ts:52-53).
review.verdict: This is a correct, secure and well-tested booking app. It meets every requirement in the brief with a coherent, phone-tested winery look. Before handing it over I would add CI, fix or remove the empty openspec reference, and add a confirmation step to staff cancellations.
